1	# Gatemap
2	
3	## What
4	2D raster sweep over an axis-aligned rectangle in `(V_tg, V_bg)`-space at
5	zero field, via `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, ..., k_bg.volt, ...)`. All lock-in
6	channels read at every grid point; gate-current channels monitored for live
7	leakage. The first map you take when cap ratios `dtg` / `dbg` are not yet
8	trusted — sweeping in raw gate voltages avoids any `(n, D) ↔ (V_tg, V_bg)`
9	calibration error. Plots via
10	`sharpelab_nb.plotting.plot_gatemap(file_path, file, nD=True)` (the analysis
11	side reprojects to physical `(n, D)` after the fact, using the cap ratios
12	in scope at plot time — separate from the sweep itself).
13	
14	For the polygon-in-`(n, D)` variant (rasterized parallelogram via
15	`raster.rasterize` + `multisweep`), see `nD-map`. The two recipes share
16	external structure (AsyncStation, fp/plot, comments) but differ in their
17	sweep call and their cap-ratio dependency.
18	
19	## When
20	Once the device-init validators are in place: hard dependency is
21	`gate-current-sanity-check` with Cell B committed (the safe `(V_tg, V_bg)`
22	ranges define the maximum extent of the megasweep box) and, for
23	rhombohedral devices, `silicon-backgate-survey` (`V_si` is held at the
24	operating point this gatemap commits to). A `gate-leakage-survey` should
25	have been done already — or, for any gatemap that ventures far from
26	`(0, 0)`, have a leakage-check `register_run_before` callback installed
27	(see `gate-leakage-survey` Flavor B). After the first gatemap is in hand,
28	the campaign branches by scientific question (see `## Next`).
29	
30	The natural predecessor of `nD-map`: a clean axis-aligned gatemap is the
31	substrate from which `cap-ratio-calibration` extracts the CNP slope, which
32	is what makes a polygon-in-`(n, D)` sweep trustworthy.
33	
34	## Why
35	The gatemap is the only measurement in the toploader pipeline that surveys
36	the gate plane densely without committing to a particular feature or to a
37	particular set of cap ratios. Every downstream Block 1 recipe targets a
38	specific point or line — and you can only pick one if you've seen the
39	map. A 201×201 megasweep at `slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1` takes ~3.5 hours
40	and is the densest first-look you can get without dropping into
41	rasterized-polygon sweeps (`nD-map`).
42	
43	The axis-aligned form has two failure modes the polygon form doesn't:
44	(1) it wastes 30–60% of points outside the safe polygon when the
45	`(n, D)` region of interest is a tilted parallelogram, and (2) on a
46	device with strongly-coupled top/bottom gates, a rectangle in
47	`(V_tg, V_bg)` is a sheared parallelogram in `(n, D)` and the CNP cuts
48	the rectangle diagonally. Both are worth tolerating on the *first* map,
49	because the alternative requires cap ratios you don't yet trust.
50	
51	## Recipe
52	
53	1. Decide the `(V_bg, V_tg)` extent. Stay strictly inside the validators
54	   set by the device-init recipes; for a first gatemap pick a rectangle
55	   that brackets the working setpoint with margin (e.g.
56	   `V_bg ∈ [-8, 6.5]`, `V_tg ∈ [-6.5, 6.5]` for a 25.5/16 nm device at
57	   `V_si = 48 V`).
58	2. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('gatemap')` first,
59	   then optional structured tags identifying the operating point, e.g.
60	   `s.add_comment(f'MC{N}, Vsi = {V_si}V')`. Call
61	   `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` if the notebook has the helper (RPL_19
62	   idiom — captures device/run state into the comments list).
63	3. `s.ramp` all relevant gates and the field to their start values.
64	   `time.sleep(10)` (or `interruptable_sleep(30)` for a slower settle when
65	   `V_si` just moved).
66	4. `fp` temperature (and `fridge_temperature` if available), all three
67	   gate currents, and every lock-in `X` and `P`. `plot` `k_bg.volt` vs
68	   `k_bg.curr` and `'time'` vs `k_tg.curr` / `k_si.curr` so live leakage
69	   is visible; for a survey gatemap also `s.plot(k_bg.volt, sr.X)` over
70	   each lock-in.
71	5. (Optional) `s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, [sr830s_2_autorange])`
72	   if you want sensitivity to track during the slow axis. Aaron typically
73	   leaves this commented out for the canonical 201×201 — autorange
74	   disturbs the lock-ins mid-fast-row.
75	6. `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(V_tg_lo, V_tg_hi, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(V_bg_lo, V_bg_hi, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`.
76	   Slow-axis convention varies — Aaron's recent style is TG slow, BG
77	   fast (cf. RPL_19/20251220 cell 70); RPL_10/241207 used BG slow, TG
78	   fast. Either works; the analysis-side `plot_gatemap(..., nD=True)`
79	   reprojects to `(n, D)` regardless.
80	7. Park gates: `k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`. (Don't park `V_si` unless
81	   you're done with this `V_si` entirely.) Send a Discord/Slack ping
82	   (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) if the alert hooks are installed.
83	
84	## Verify
85	
86	Post-hoc disk checks. The map's `data/<file_id>/` directory has
87	`metadata.json`, `data.tsv.gz`, and `plot.png`. The `Run` loader unrolls
88	the 2D megasweep into flat rows, so column-wise statistics work the same
89	way they do for 1D sweeps.
90	
91	```python
92	from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
93	import numpy as np
94	
95	run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
96	print(summarize_run(run))
97	# expect: type 2D, recipe 'gatemap', complete (rows == n_slow * n_fast),
98	#         tags carrying MC label / Vsi.
99	
100	# 1. Sweep completeness — interrupted sweeps usually mean leakage abort or
101	#    operator stop; treat as block until the human explains.
102	assert not run.interrupted, "sweep was interrupted; investigate before advancing"
103	
104	# 2. Leakage stayed below threshold across the whole map. Threshold matches
105	#    the gate-leakage-survey abort thresholds (~5e-11 to 8e-11 A); use 1 nA
106	#    as a soft ceiling and surface anything closer than 100 pA.
107	i_tg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_tg_curr")).max()
108	i_bg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_bg_curr")).max()
109	assert i_tg_max < 1e-9 and i_bg_max < 1e-9, (
110	    f"leakage exceeded 1 nA: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}"
111	)
112	if max(i_tg_max, i_bg_max) > 1e-10:
113	    print(f"⚠️  approaching leakage threshold: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}")
114	
115	# 3. Lock-in channels not stuck or saturated. Flat-zero or flat-nonzero on
116	#    every channel is the grounded-device failure mode (cf. gate-current-
117	#    sanity-check failure-mode catalog); flat anything is suspicious for a
118	#    map that's supposed to vary across (V_tg, V_bg).
119	for name in ("sr830_1_X", "sr830_2_X", "sr830_3_X", "sr830_4_X"):
120	    if name not in run.cols:
121	        continue
122	    x = run.col(name)
123	    if np.allclose(x, x[0]):
124	        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} is flat across the map — check lock-in / wiring")
125	    if np.isnan(x).any():
126	        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} has NaNs — sweep aborted mid-row?")
127	
128	# 4. Eyeball the rendered plot — Read('<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>/plot.png').
129	#    The gatemap's qualitative features (CNP line slope, dome shapes, flavor
130	#    transitions) are easier to assess visually than numerically; the
131	#    numeric checks above are necessary, not sufficient.
132	```
133	
134	If a CNP-line extraction or feature catalog is needed downstream, defer
135	that to `gatemap-feature-locator` (separate recipe). The Verify block
136	here is just "is this map clean enough to advance from".
137	
138	## Examples
139	- `aaron/RPL_19/20251220_measure.ipynb` cells 69–76 — canonical mature
140	  form. Cell 70 is the 201×201
141	  `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(-6.5, 6.5, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(-8, 6.5, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`
142	  at `V_si = 48 V` using `mc_9`; cell 71 reverses the slow axis (sweep
143	  direction check). Cell 72 is a markdown interlude ("THink there is a
144	  problem with a bnc t so swapping that out"); cell 73 retries cell 71's
145	  range. Cells 74–75 are silicon-backgate-survey forms (`V_si` as slow
146	  axis with `np.linspace(48, -48, 101)` — strictly belongs to
147	  `silicon-backgate-survey`, included here because the same `# Gatemap`
148	  markdown header parents them). Cell 76 is the same 201×201 at
149	  `V_si = -48 V`. The `add_comment('MC6, Vsi = -48V, gate map')` plus
150	  `add_comment(grab_metadata())` is the canonical comment idiom; this
151	  recipe's slug is now `gatemap` rather than the older `'gate map'`
152	  freeform string.
153	- `aaron/RPL_10/241207_measure.ipynb` cells 43–53 — first-cooldown form,
154	  predates the mature shape. Cell 43 is the markdown header; cells 44–53
155	  are 10 megasweeps over progressively-refined `(V_tg, V_bg)` rectangles
156	  at `V_si = +10, -10, +20 V`. Cell 44 omits the `s.ramp(k_si.volt, ...)`
157	  (V_si already at default); cells 46–47 add the explicit ramp + sleep.
158	  Cell 48 is `V_si = -10 V`; cells 51–53 are `V_si = +20 V`. Notable:

# Gatemap

## What
2D raster sweep over an axis-aligned rectangle in `(V_tg, V_bg)`-space at
zero field, via `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, ..., k_bg.volt, ...)`. All lock-in
channels read at every grid point; gate-current channels monitored for live
leakage. The first map you take when cap ratios `dtg` / `dbg` are not yet
trusted — sweeping in raw gate voltages avoids any `(n, D) ↔ (V_tg, V_bg)`
calibration error. Plots via
`sharpelab_nb.plotting.plot_gatemap(file_path, file, nD=True)` (the analysis
side reprojects to physical `(n, D)` after the fact, using the cap ratios
in scope at plot time — separate from the sweep itself).

For the polygon-in-`(n, D)` variant (rasterized parallelogram via
`raster.rasterize` + `multisweep`), see `nD-map`. The two recipes share
external structure (AsyncStation, fp/plot, comments) but differ in their
sweep call and their cap-ratio dependency.

## When
Once the device-init validators are in place: hard dependency is
`gate-current-sanity-check` with Cell B committed (the safe `(V_tg, V_bg)`
ranges define the maximum extent of the megasweep box) and, for
rhombohedral devices, `silicon-backgate-survey` (`V_si` is held at the
operating point this gatemap commits to). A `gate-leakage-survey` should
have been done already — or, for any gatemap that ventures far from
`(0, 0)`, have a leakage-check `register_run_before` callback installed
(see `gate-leakage-survey` Flavor B). After the first gatemap is in hand,
the campaign branches by scientific question (see `## Next`).

The natural predecessor of `nD-map`: a clean axis-aligned gatemap is the
substrate from which `cap-ratio-calibration` extracts the CNP slope, which
is what makes a polygon-in-`(n, D)` sweep trustworthy.

## Why
The gatemap is the only measurement in the toploader pipeline that surveys
the gate plane densely without committing to a particular feature or to a
particular set of cap ratios. Every downstream Block 1 recipe targets a
specific point or line — and you can only pick one if you've seen the
map. A 201×201 megasweep at `slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1` takes ~3.5 hours
and is the densest first-look you can get without dropping into
rasterized-polygon sweeps (`nD-map`).

The axis-aligned form has two failure modes the polygon form doesn't:
(1) it wastes 30–60% of points outside the safe polygon when the
`(n, D)` region of interest is a tilted parallelogram, and (2) on a
device with strongly-coupled top/bottom gates, a rectangle in
`(V_tg, V_bg)` is a sheared parallelogram in `(n, D)` and the CNP cuts
the rectangle diagonally. Both are worth tolerating on the *first* map,
because the alternative requires cap ratios you don't yet trust.

## Recipe

1. Decide the `(V_bg, V_tg)` extent. Stay strictly inside the validators
   set by the device-init recipes; for a first gatemap pick a rectangle
   that brackets the working setpoint with margin (e.g.
   `V_bg ∈ [-8, 6.5]`, `V_tg ∈ [-6.5, 6.5]` for a 25.5/16 nm device at
   `V_si = 48 V`).
2. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('gatemap')` first,
   then optional structured tags identifying the operating point, e.g.
   `s.add_comment(f'MC{N}, Vsi = {V_si}V')`. Call
   `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` if the notebook has the helper (RPL_19
   idiom — captures device/run state into the comments list).
3. `s.ramp` all relevant gates and the field to their start values.
   `time.sleep(10)` (or `interruptable_sleep(30)` for a slower settle when
   `V_si` just moved).
4. `fp` temperature (and `fridge_temperature` if available), all three
   gate currents, and every lock-in `X` and `P`. `plot` `k_bg.volt` vs
   `k_bg.curr` and `'time'` vs `k_tg.curr` / `k_si.curr` so live leakage
   is visible; for a survey gatemap also `s.plot(k_bg.volt, sr.X)` over
   each lock-in.
5. (Optional) `s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, [sr830s_2_autorange])`
   if you want sensitivity to track during the slow axis. Aaron typically
   leaves this commented out for the canonical 201×201 — autorange
   disturbs the lock-ins mid-fast-row.
6. `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(V_tg_lo, V_tg_hi, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(V_bg_lo, V_bg_hi, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`.
   Slow-axis convention varies — Aaron's recent style is TG slow, BG
   fast (cf. RPL_19/20251220 cell 70); RPL_10/241207 used BG slow, TG
   fast. Either works; the analysis-side `plot_gatemap(..., nD=True)`
   reprojects to `(n, D)` regardless.
7. Park gates: `k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`. (Don't park `V_si` unless
   you're done with this `V_si` entirely.) Send a Discord/Slack ping
   (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) if the alert hooks are installed.

## Verify

Post-hoc disk checks. The map's `data/<file_id>/` directory has
`metadata.json`, `data.tsv.gz`, and `plot.png`. The `Run` loader unrolls
the 2D megasweep into flat rows, so column-wise statistics work the same
way they do for 1D sweeps.

```python
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
import numpy as np

run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
print(summarize_run(run))
# expect: type 2D, recipe 'gatemap', complete (rows == n_slow * n_fast),
#         tags carrying MC label / Vsi.

# 1. Sweep completeness — interrupted sweeps usually mean leakage abort or
#    operator stop; treat as block until the human explains.
assert not run.interrupted, "sweep was interrupted; investigate before advancing"

# 2. Leakage stayed below threshold across the whole map. Threshold matches
#    the gate-leakage-survey abort thresholds (~5e-11 to 8e-11 A); use 1 nA
#    as a soft ceiling and surface anything closer than 100 pA.
i_tg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_tg_curr")).max()
i_bg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_bg_curr")).max()
assert i_tg_max < 1e-9 and i_bg_max < 1e-9, (
    f"leakage exceeded 1 nA: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}"
)
if max(i_tg_max, i_bg_max) > 1e-10:
    print(f"⚠️  approaching leakage threshold: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}")

# 3. Lock-in channels not stuck or saturated. Flat-zero or flat-nonzero on
#    every channel is the grounded-device failure mode (cf. gate-current-
#    sanity-check failure-mode catalog); flat anything is suspicious for a
#    map that's supposed to vary across (V_tg, V_bg).
for name in ("sr830_1_X", "sr830_2_X", "sr830_3_X", "sr830_4_X"):
    if name not in run.cols:
        continue
    x = run.col(name)
    if np.allclose(x, x[0]):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} is flat across the map — check lock-in / wiring")
    if np.isnan(x).any():
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} has NaNs — sweep aborted mid-row?")

# 4. Eyeball the rendered plot — Read('<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>/plot.png').
#    The gatemap's qualitative features (CNP line slope, dome shapes, flavor
#    transitions) are easier to assess visually than numerically; the
#    numeric checks above are necessary, not sufficient.
```

If a CNP-line extraction or feature catalog is needed downstream, defer
that to `gatemap-feature-locator` (separate recipe). The Verify block
here is just "is this map clean enough to advance from".

## Examples
- `aaron/RPL_19/20251220_measure.ipynb` cells 69–76 — canonical mature
  form. Cell 70 is the 201×201
  `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(-6.5, 6.5, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(-8, 6.5, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`
  at `V_si = 48 V` using `mc_9`; cell 71 reverses the slow axis (sweep
  direction check). Cell 72 is a markdown interlude ("THink there is a
  problem with a bnc t so swapping that out"); cell 73 retries cell 71's
  range. Cells 74–75 are silicon-backgate-survey forms (`V_si` as slow
  axis with `np.linspace(48, -48, 101)` — strictly belongs to
  `silicon-backgate-survey`, included here because the same `# Gatemap`
  markdown header parents them). Cell 76 is the same 201×201 at
  `V_si = -48 V`. The `add_comment('MC6, Vsi = -48V, gate map')` plus
  `add_comment(grab_metadata())` is the canonical comment idiom; this
  recipe's slug is now `gatemap` rather than the older `'gate map'`
  freeform string.
- `aaron/RPL_10/241207_measure.ipynb` cells 43–53 — first-cooldown form,
  predates the mature shape. Cell 43 is the markdown header; cells 44–53
  are 10 megasweeps over progressively-refined `(V_tg, V_bg)` rectangles
  at `V_si = +10, -10, +20 V`. Cell 44 omits the `s.ramp(k_si.volt, ...)`
  (V_si already at default); cells 46–47 add the explicit ramp + sleep.
  Cell 48 is `V_si = -10 V`; cells 51–53 are `V_si = +20 V`. Notable:
  each cell carries `s.add_comment('initial gatemap, V_si = 10')` —
  Aaron's `add_comment` discipline begins exactly here in this notebook
  (gate-checks at cells 22–42 had none). The autorange callback is
  commented out for these runs.

## Next
Default branches by what you saw on the map:
- **Cap ratios not yet trusted (or first cooldown of this device)**:
  `cap-ratio-calibration` — extract CNP slope from this gatemap, refine
  `dtg` / `dbg`. Required before any `nD-map` you want to trust.
- **Caps already trusted, want a denser polygon survey**: `nD-map` over
  the `(n, D)` parallelogram of interest.
- **No clear features at this V_si**: revisit `silicon-backgate-survey`
  for a different operating point.
- **Features visible, want them at finite field**: `gatemap-in-field`
  (the same shape with `s.ramp(mag.field, B)` first; bake settling time
  in for a strong magnet).
- **Specific point looks SC / AHC / flavor-transition-shaped**:
  `field-sweep-1d` to characterize how that feature responds to B at
  fixed gate; `gate-axis-linecut` for a denser 1D cut along an n- or
  D-line through the feature.
- **Suspect history dependence (asymmetric or noisy-looking gatemap)**:
  `hysteresis-check` along an n-line through the feature.
- **Want a ranked list of candidate features to follow up**:
  `gatemap-feature-locator` (HERA-side analysis).

Block 2 branches once Block 1 is exhausted: `landau-fan` (B × n at
fixed D), `temperature-dependence`; deferred: `fraunhofer` (B × bias at
fixed gate), `bias-spectroscopy`. Reach for these only after the
zero-field map is well-characterized.

# Gate current sanity check

## What
Probe each active gate from 0 V outward in both polarities, in iterative
sweeps a human refines between runs, until the safe range for the cooldown
is established. Three things at once: (1) the device passes a measurable
lock-in current, (2) each gate's leakage onset is found at pA resolution,
and (3) the resulting validators capture the safe range as a hard limit for
the rest of the cooldown. Combines what used to be a separate "liveness
check" and "range-finding" into a single iterate-then-bless loop because
that's how it actually plays out at the bench.

## When
Once per cooldown, after instrument init and the measurement-config block,
before any subsequent recipe. Optionally also after thermal cycling or
physical intervention (reseating contacts, swapping a bias source).

**Precondition**: device must be ungrounded. A device tied to ground at any
contact gives flat-nonzero, all-channels-identical lock-in `X` readouts
that look like signal but aren't (see failure-mode catalog). Confirm before
running.

## Why
A device that doesn't pass current at gates parked at zero, or a gate that
leaks at small voltage, is not going to give a clean gatemap — find this in
30 seconds, save an hour. Beyond liveness, this is where the cooldown-wide
validators get **set from observed safe range** rather than guessed from
geometry. Validators set this way are the only durable record of "I
confirmed this range is safe": they gate every subsequent recipe in the
session, and the values get mirrored to the device card so they survive
into the next session (kernel resets typically mean a fresh notebook —
the device is ungrounded during measurements, so restarts aren't free).

## Recipe

Two cells. The agent proposes both together; the human runs Cell A
repeatedly (one cell per iteration — copy the cell to make a new run rather
than re-running in place, so the history of the search stays in the
notebook), then runs Cell B once at the end.

### Cell A — iterative sweep

Sweeps one gate over one polarity with all other gates parked at 0 and
`nplci=10` on the gate-current channels for high-SNR pA readback. `nplci`
stays at 10 across every iteration; Cell B resets it. Edit the block at
the top per iteration; copy the cell for the next run:

```python
# === EDIT THIS BLOCK BETWEEN RUNS (or copy-and-edit the cell) ===
gate = k_tg          # k_tg | k_bg | k_si
v_endpoint = +1.0    # walk this out per polarity until leakage shows
n_pts = 51
delay = 1            # s
lockins = [sr830_1, sr830_2, sr830_3, sr830_4]   # match your mc
# ================================================================

# nplci=10 across the gate-current channels for ~pA-floor readback (~167 ms / pt).
# Stays at 10 across every iteration; Cell B resets it back to 1.
k_tg.nplci(10)
k_bg.nplci(10)
# k_si.nplci(10)  # if applicable

s = sweep.AsyncStation(measurement_config)
s.add_comment('gate-current-sanity-check')
s.add_comment(f'gate: {gate.name}')
s.add_comment(f'leg: 0 -> {v_endpoint:+g} V')

s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0)

s.fp(temperature)
s.fp(k_tg.volt).fp(k_tg.curr)
s.fp(k_bg.volt).fp(k_bg.curr)
for lia in lockins:
    s.fp(lia.X).fp(lia.P)

xp = gate.volt
s.plot(xp, k_tg.curr)
s.plot(xp, k_bg.curr)
for lia in lockins:
    s.plot(xp, lia.X)

try:
    s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_endpoint, n_pts), delay=delay)

    s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)
```

The `lockins` list should match the channels in your `measurement_config`.
If `mc` makes the active set unambiguous (e.g. it lists exactly four
sr830s), HERA may pre-fill the list; otherwise leave it for the human to
set per session.

- Start: `gate = k_tg`, `v_endpoint = +1.0`, `n_pts = 51`. Run.
- Watch the live plot. Three things to read:
  - Lock-in `X` channels: nonzero, smoothly varying → device alive.
  - `k_tg.curr` (active gate): stays in pA → no leakage in this range.
  - `k_bg.curr` (parked gate): at the readback floor → no cross-gate path.

  the copy, run (e.g. 1 → 3 → 6 V).

parks the gate.

A geometry-derived ceiling (≈ ±0.5 V/nm × hBN thickness for the metal
gates) is a sanity ceiling: don't walk `|v_endpoint|` past it even if
leakage hasn't shown — assume something else is masking the readback.

### Cell B — commit validators

After both polarities of every gate have a confirmed safe range, lock the
live validators and reset gate-current `nplci` back to its standard value:

```python
# Commit validators at the safe ranges established by Cell A iterations,
# and reset gate-current nplci back to its standard value.
k_tg.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(-V_neg_tg, +V_pos_tg)
k_bg.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(-V_neg_bg, +V_pos_bg)
# k_si.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(-V_neg_si, +V_pos_si)  # if applicable

k_tg.nplci(1)
k_bg.nplci(1)
# k_si.nplci(1)

print('k_tg.volt validator:', k_tg.volt.vals)
print('k_bg.volt validator:', k_bg.volt.vals)
```

older `remove_validator(); add_validator(...)` two-step.

record. (Cell 1's `GATES["..."]["limit"]` isn't the right surface; kernel
resets are typically a new notebook anyway.)

but **does not propose any subsequent recipe step until the human reports
the discovered ranges and the validator cell has been run**. Asking for
the limits is the explicit handshake. Human is the gate; HERA waits.

# === Gate C — provided-contact liveness scout (first-session branch) ===
# Route the provided contact config, confirm contacts alive + device passes
# current, and scout the CNP along a 1D TG sweep at B=0, BG=Si=0. No
# references this session -> qualitative liveness (reentry-baseline
# first-session branch), not a quantitative reentry comparison.

# --- Preconditions (state this cell assumes but does not set) ---
assert abs(magnet.mag()) < 0.01, f"field not ~0 T: {magnet.mag()}"
assert heater.sample_temperature() < 2.0, f"T not at base: {heater.sample_temperature()}"
print("pre: B =", magnet.mag(), "T ;  T =", heater.sample_temperature(), "K")
print("pre: BG =", k_bg.volt(), "V ;  Si =", k_2410.volt(), "V ;  TG =", k_tg.voltage(), "V")

# --- Route the provided contact configuration ---
mux.select({"source": "T2", "drain": "T7",
            "sr1+": "T3", "sr1-": "T4",
            "sr2+": "B4", "sr2-": "B5",
            "sr3+": "T5", "sr3-": "B6"})
print("mux: source T2, drain T7 | sr1 T3-T4 | sr2 B4-B5 | sr3 T5-B6")

# --- Per-run measurement config (real contact labels + comment) ---
mc = dict(meas_config)
mc["sr0"] = "drain current on T7"
mc["sr1"] = "Rxx T3-T4"
mc["sr2"] = "Rxx B4-B5"
mc["sr3"] = "Rxy T5-B6"
mc["comments"] = "Gate C liveness scout: 1D TG sweep -5.9->+6.9 V, BG=Si=0, B=0"

s = async_station(mc)
s.add_comment('reentry-baseline')
s.add_comment('gate-C liveness scout, first-session branch (no references)')
s.add_comment('TG sweep -5.9 -> +6.9 V, BG=0, Si=0, B=0')

# Park BG/Si at 0; start TG at the hole end (smooth DC205 ramp from current V).
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
s.ramp(k_2410.volt, 0)

# Monitor: Keithley gate-leakage currents + all lock-in X/P.
s.fp(k_bg.curr).fp(k_2410.curr)
for sr in [sr0, sr1, sr2, sr3]:
    s.fp(sr.X).fp(sr.P)

s.plot(dc205_volt, sr0.X)  # live drain current

try:

finally:
    s.ramp(dc205_volt, 0)
print("done; TG parked at 0 V")

import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run

run = open_run("data/0")
print(summarize_run(run))
print("interrupted:", run.interrupted)
print("cols:", list(run.cols))

vtg = run.col("DC_bias")
I = run.col("sr0_X") / (-1e6)          # current channel, gain -1e6
I_bias = 5e-9

def R(name):
    return run.col(name) / I_bias

# Leakage
for c in run.cols:
    if "curr" in c.lower():
        print(f"leak {c}: max|I| = {np.abs(run.col(c)).max():.3e} A")

print("I (drain) med/min/max nA:", np.median(I)*1e9, I.min()*1e9, I.max()*1e9)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(7, 7), sharex=True)
for nm, col in [("sr1 Rxx T3-T4","sr1_X"), ("sr2 Rxx B4-B5","sr2_X")]:
    r = R(col)
    icnp = np.argmax(r)
    print(f"{nm}: Rxx peak {r[icnp]:.1f} ohm at DC_bias = {vtg[icnp]:.3f} V "
          f"(edge med ~{np.median(r[:10]):.1f}/{np.median(r[-10:]):.1f} ohm)")
    ax[0].plot(vtg, r, label=nm)
ax[0].set_ylabel("Rxx (ohm)"); ax[0].legend(); ax[0].grid(alpha=.3)
ax[0].set_title("Gate C scout — file_id 0, BG=Si=0, B=0")

rxy = R("sr3_X")
ax[1].plot(vtg, rxy, label="sr3 Rxy T5-B6", color="C2")
ax[1].axhline(0, color="k", lw=.5)
ax[1].set_ylabel("Rxy (ohm)"); ax[1].set_xlabel("DC_bias / TG (V)")
ax[1].legend(); ax[1].grid(alpha=.3)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/gateC_scout.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/gateC_scout.png")

# === Step 1 — 0 T (n,D) gate map (gatemap.md) ===
# Gate-C scout put the CNP at (TG,BG) ~ (0,0), Si=0. Map the full CNP line
# across the gate window to fit the cap ratio (cnp-and-dline-calibration:
# c_bg/c_tg = -slope) and pick clean hole/electron regions + the D=0 line.
# Geometry-prior slope ~-1.3 -> CNP reaches TG ~ +/-5.2 over BG +/-4, so the
# TG[-5.95,5.95] x BG[-4,4] box brackets it with margin.

# --- Preconditions (assumed, not set here) ---
assert abs(magnet.mag()) < 0.01, f"field not ~0 T: {magnet.mag()}"
assert heater.sample_temperature() < 2.0, f"T not at base: {heater.sample_temperature()}"
print("pre: B =", magnet.mag(), "T ;  T =", heater.sample_temperature(),
      "K ;  Si =", k_2410.volt(), "V")

# --- Per-run config (fresh station -> no stale scout comments) ---
mc = dict(meas_config)
mc["sr0"] = "drain current on T7"
mc["sr1"] = "Rxx T3-T4"
mc["sr2"] = "Rxx B4-B5"
mc["sr3"] = "Rxy T5-B6"
mc["comments"] = "Step1 gatemap: TG[-5.95,5.95]x101 fast x BG[-4,4]x41 slow, Si=0, B=0"

s = async_station(mc)
s.add_comment('gatemap')
s.add_comment('Step1 0T (n,D) map; Si=0; Gate-C scout (file 0) put CNP ~(0,0)')
s.add_comment('fast DC_bias/TG [-5.95,5.95]x101; slow BG [-4,4]x41; slow_delay3 fast_delay1')

# Position slow axis + Si; fast axis (DC205) is positioned by the megasweep.
s.ramp(k_2410.volt, 0)
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, -4)

# Monitor: gate leakage + all lock-in X/P.
s.fp(k_bg.curr).fp(k_2410.curr)
for sr in [sr0, sr1, sr2, sr3]:
    s.fp(sr.X).fp(sr.P)

s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)   # live leakage
s.plot(dc205_volt, sr0.X)      # live current

try:
    s.megasweep(k_bg.volt, np.linspace(-4, 4, 41),
                dc205_volt, np.linspace(-5.95, 5.95, 101),
                slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)
finally:
    s.ramp(dc205_volt, 0)
    s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
print("done; gates parked at 0")

try:
        async with NbModelClient(ws_url, path=rel_path, ws_max_body_size=WS_MAX_BODY_SIZE) as client:
            await client.wait_until_synced()
            _require_policy(client, EXECUTE_POLICIES, "execute-cell")

            cell, idx = _find_cell_by_id(client, cell_id)
            if cell is None:
                sys.exit(f"error: cell id not found: {cell_id}")
            if cell.get("cell_type") != "code":
                sys.exit(f"error: cell @ {idx} is not a code cell (type={cell.get('cell_type')!r})")

            kernel_id = _find_or_create_kernel(server_url, token, rel_path)
            conn = _kernel_connection_file(kernel_id)
            if not conn.exists():
                sys.exit(
                    f"error: kernel connection file not found at {conn}; "
                    f"check JUPYTER_RUNTIME_DIR alignment between nb-collab and JupyterLab."
                )

            print(f"connected: {server_url} path={rel_path} cells={len(client)}")
            print(f"  executing code @ {idx} id={cell_id} kernel={kernel_id}")

            kc = BlockingKernelClient()
            kc.load_connection_file(str(conn))
            kc.start_channels()
            try:
                kc.wait_for_ready(timeout=DEFAULT_KERNEL_READY_TIMEOUT)
                result = client.execute_cell(idx, kc, timeout=timeout)
            finally:
                kc.stop_channels()

            # Records when nb-collab fired the run. recordTiming (if enabled
            # on the server) independently stamps precise kernel start/end
            # under cell.metadata.execution; this is the agent-side marker.
            _stamp_cell_event(client, idx, "executed_at", _utc_now_iso())

            # Re-read the cell so the printed tail reflects the YDoc state
            # the operator will see (matches what `wait` emits).
            cell, _ = _find_cell_by_id(client, cell_id)
            status = result.get("status", "?")
            print(f"status: {status if status != 'ok' else 'done'}")
            print(f"execution_count: {_fmt_exec_count(result.get('execution_count'))}")
            tail = _format_output_tail((cell or {}).get("outputs", []) if cell else [])
            if tail:
                print("--- output ---")
                sys.stdout.write(tail)
                if not tail.endswith("\n"):
                    print()
            return EXIT_OK if status == "ok" else EXIT_ERROR
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as e:
        sys.exit(f"error: execute-cell failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e})")

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	B=0 Fermi-surface counting: ABA vs ABC trilayer graphene.
4	
5	Tests the stacking-extraction premise (docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md):
6	  ABA -> >=2 distinct Fermi surfaces (ML Dirac + BL parabolic, coexisting)
7	  ABC -> 1 Fermi surface at high n (after the trigonal-warping Lifshitz cascade)
8	
9	ABA: continuum 6-site SWMcC Hamiltonian (Datta params; gamma3=gamma4=0 -> isotropic),
10	     same parameters as hera/models/aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py.
11	ABC: MacDonald PRB 82,035409 (2010) effective 2-band model (Eq.6/7), with
12	     trigonal warping (gamma3) -> the 3-pocket->annulus->single cascade.
13	
14	Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (hbar/2 pi e) * A_k.
15	No external deps beyond numpy/scipy.
16	Run: uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy python3 fs_count_b0.py
17	"""
18	import numpy as np
19	import scipy.constants as cst
20	from scipy.ndimage import label
21	
22	HBAR, E = cst.hbar, cst.e
23	A0 = 0.246e-9
24	
25	def F_from_area(A_k):
26	    """Onsager frequency (Tesla) from a k-space area (1/m^2)."""
27	    return HBAR * A_k / (2 * np.pi * E)
28	
29	# ---------------- ABA: continuum 6-site SWMcC ----------------
30	G0, G1, G2, G5, DELTA = 3.1, 0.39, -0.028, 0.01, 0.021   # eV (Datta)
31	VF = np.sqrt(3)/2 * A0 * (G0 * E) / HBAR                  # m/s
32	
33	def H_aba(k, U=0.0):
34	    """6x6 ABA Hamiltonian (eV) at |k| (1/m), isotropic (g3=g4=0).
35	    Basis A1,B1,A2,B2,A3,B3. U = layer potential (eV) for displacement field."""
36	    w = HBAR * VF * k / E                                 # intralayer Dirac, eV
37	    H = np.zeros((6, 6))
38	    # on-site: delta on dimers B1,A2,B3 ; layer potential +U,0,-U
39	    diag = np.array([0,0,0,0,0,0], float)
40	    for s in (1,2,5): diag[s] += DELTA
41	    for s in (0,1): diag[s] += U
42	    for s in (4,5): diag[s] -= U
43	    np.fill_diagonal(H, diag)
44	    # intralayer Dirac A_i-B_i
45	    for a,b in ((0,1),(2,3),(4,5)): H[a,b]=H[b,a]=w
46	    # interlayer constants
47	    for s1,s2,v in ((1,2,G1),(2,5,G1),(0,4,G2/2),(1,5,G5/2)): H[s1,s2]=H[s2,s1]=v
48	    return H
49	
50	def aba_bands(kgrid, U=0.0):
51	    """Return E[band, k] for conduction-relevant bands (all 6)."""
52	    return np.array([np.linalg.eigvalsh(H_aba(k, U)) for k in kgrid]).T
53	
54	def aba_fs(n_target, U=0.0, kmax=6e8, nk=6000):
55	    """Find E_F for electron density n_target (m^-2); return (E_F, list of (F,kF) per FS).
56	    E_F search capped at 70 meV: density n(E_F) is monotonic there and covers n up to
57	    ~3.5e12; beyond that the heavy BL pocket's k_F approaches kmax and the curve folds."""
58	    kg = np.linspace(1e3, kmax, nk)
59	    Eb = aba_bands(kg, U)                                  # (6, nk) eV
60	    # density vs E_F: n(E_F)=sum_bands k_F^2/pi (g_s g_v = 4)
61	    EFs = np.linspace(0, 0.07, 1500)
62	    def density(EF):
63	        tot = 0.0
64	        for b in range(6):
65	            cross = np.where((Eb[b,:-1]-EF)*(Eb[b,1:]-EF) < 0)[0]
66	            for c in cross:
67	                kF = kg[c]
68	                # only electron pockets (band rising through EF)
69	                if Eb[b,c+1] > Eb[b,c]:
70	                    tot += kF**2/np.pi
71	        return tot
72	    nvals = np.array([density(ef) for ef in EFs])
73	    EF = np.interp(n_target, nvals, EFs)
74	    # extract FS at EF
75	    fs = []
76	    for b in range(6):
77	        cross = np.where((Eb[b,:-1]-EF)*(Eb[b,1:]-EF) < 0)[0]
78	        for c in cross:
79	            if Eb[b,c+1] > Eb[b,c]:
80	                kF = kg[c]
81	                fs.append((F_from_area(np.pi*kF**2), kF))
82	    return EF, sorted(fs)
83	
84	# ---------------- ABC: MacDonald effective 2-band ----------------
85	# Table I (ABC trilayer): gamma0 set to 3.16 to fix energy scale
86	G0c, G1c, G2c, G3c, G4c, DELTAc = 3.16, 0.502, -0.0171, -0.377, -0.099, -0.0014  # eV
87	def vi(g): return np.sqrt(3)/2 * A0 * (g*E)/HBAR
88	V0,V3,V4 = vi(G0c), vi(G3c), vi(G4c)
89	
90	def E_abc(kx, ky, ud=0.0):
91	    """ABC conduction-band energy E^+ (eV) at (kx,ky). ud = displacement (eV)."""
92	    p = HBAR*np.hypot(kx,ky)/E            # eV*s/m units folded: treat v*p in eV
93	    phi = np.arctan2(ky, kx)
94	    vp = V0*HBAR*np.hypot(kx,ky)/E        # v0*p in eV
95	    h_ch = vp**3 / G1c**2
96	    h_s  = DELTAc - 2*V0*V4*(HBAR*np.hypot(kx,ky)/E)**2/G1c
97	    h_tr = G2c/2 - 2*V0*V3*(HBAR*np.hypot(kx,ky)/E)**2/G1c
98	    h_gap = ud*(1 - (vp/G1c)**2)
99	    root = np.sqrt(h_ch**2 + h_tr**2 + h_gap**2 + 2*np.cos(3*phi)*h_ch*h_tr)
100	    return h_s + root
101	
102	def abc_fs(n_target, ud=0.0, kmax=3e8, ng=601):
103	    """Count ABC FS topology + frequencies at density n_target (m^-2)."""
104	    kx = np.linspace(-kmax, kmax, ng); KX,KY = np.meshgrid(kx, kx)
105	    Egrid = E_abc(KX, KY, ud)
106	    dk = kx[1]-kx[0]
107	    # find EF: occupied area * (g/(2pi)^2) = n ; g=4
108	    EFs = np.linspace(Egrid.min(), Egrid.min()+0.05, 1500)
109	    areas = []
110	    for ef in EFs:
111	        occ = Egrid < ef
112	        areas.append(occ.sum()*dk*dk)
113	    nvals = 4*np.array(areas)/(2*np.pi)**2
114	    EF = np.interp(n_target, nvals, EFs)
115	    occ = Egrid < EF
116	    ncc, _ = label(occ)
117	    n_components = ncc.max()
118	    center_occ = occ[ng//2, ng//2]
119	    A_occ = occ.sum()*dk*dk
120	    # topology -> n distinct frequencies
121	    if center_occ and n_components == 1:
122	        topo, nfreq = "single", 1
123	    elif (not center_occ) and n_components == 1:
124	        topo, nfreq = "annulus", 2
125	    else:
126	        topo, nfreq = f"{n_components}-pocket", 1
127	    # representative frequency from total enclosed area (single pocket case)
128	    F_tot = F_from_area(A_occ)
129	    return EF, topo, n_components, nfreq, F_tot
130	
131	# ---------------- run ----------------
132	if __name__ == "__main__":
133	    print(f"VF(ABA) = {VF:.3e} m/s ; v0(ABC) = {V0:.3e} m/s\n")
134	    ns = np.array([0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0]) * 1e12 * 1e4   # m^-2
135	    print("=== ABA (D=0) ===  n[1e12]  EF[meV]  #FS  frequencies[T] (sorted)   sum[T]")
136	    for n in ns:
137	        EF, fs = aba_fs(n)
138	        freqs = [F for F,_ in fs]
139	        fstr = ", ".join(f"{F:5.1f}" for F in freqs)
140	        print(f"   {n/1e16:5.2f}     {EF*1e3:6.1f}   {len(fs)}   [{fstr}]   {sum(freqs):5.1f}")
141	    print("\n=== ABC (D=0) ===  n[1e12]  EF[meV]  topo        #cc  #freq  F_tot[T]")
142	    for n in ns:
143	        EF, topo, ncc, nfreq, Ft = abc_fs(n)
144	        print(f"   {n/1e16:5.2f}     {EF*1e3:6.1f}   {topo:10s}  {ncc}    {nfreq}     {Ft:5.1f}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
B=0 Fermi-surface counting: ABA vs ABC trilayer graphene.

Tests the stacking-extraction premise (docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md):
  ABA -> >=2 distinct Fermi surfaces (ML Dirac + BL parabolic, coexisting)
  ABC -> 1 Fermi surface at high n (after the trigonal-warping Lifshitz cascade)

ABA: continuum 6-site SWMcC Hamiltonian (Datta params; gamma3=gamma4=0 -> isotropic),
     same parameters as hera/models/aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py.
ABC: MacDonald PRB 82,035409 (2010) effective 2-band model (Eq.6/7), with
     trigonal warping (gamma3) -> the 3-pocket->annulus->single cascade.

Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (hbar/2 pi e) * A_k.
No external deps beyond numpy/scipy.
Run: uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy python3 fs_count_b0.py
"""
import numpy as np
import scipy.constants as cst
from scipy.ndimage import label

HBAR, E = cst.hbar, cst.e
A0 = 0.246e-9

def F_from_area(A_k):
    """Onsager frequency (Tesla) from a k-space area (1/m^2)."""
    return HBAR * A_k / (2 * np.pi * E)

# ---------------- ABA: continuum 6-site SWMcC ----------------
G0, G1, G2, G5, DELTA = 3.1, 0.39, -0.028, 0.01, 0.021   # eV (Datta)
VF = np.sqrt(3)/2 * A0 * (G0 * E) / HBAR                  # m/s

def H_aba(k, U=0.0):
    """6x6 ABA Hamiltonian (eV) at |k| (1/m), isotropic (g3=g4=0).
    Basis A1,B1,A2,B2,A3,B3. U = layer potential (eV) for displacement field."""
    w = HBAR * VF * k / E                                 # intralayer Dirac, eV
    H = np.zeros((6, 6))
    # on-site: delta on dimers B1,A2,B3 ; layer potential +U,0,-U
    diag = np.array([0,0,0,0,0,0], float)
    for s in (1,2,5): diag[s] += DELTA
    for s in (0,1): diag[s] += U
    for s in (4,5): diag[s] -= U
    np.fill_diagonal(H, diag)
    # intralayer Dirac A_i-B_i
    for a,b in ((0,1),(2,3),(4,5)): H[a,b]=H[b,a]=w
    # interlayer constants
    for s1,s2,v in ((1,2,G1),(2,5,G1),(0,4,G2/2),(1,5,G5/2)): H[s1,s2]=H[s2,s1]=v
    return H

def aba_bands(kgrid, U=0.0):
    """Return E[band, k] for conduction-relevant bands (all 6)."""
    return np.array([np.linalg.eigvalsh(H_aba(k, U)) for k in kgrid]).T

def aba_fs(n_target, U=0.0, kmax=6e8, nk=6000):
    """Find E_F for electron density n_target (m^-2); return (E_F, list of (F,kF) per FS).
    E_F search capped at 70 meV: density n(E_F) is monotonic there and covers n up to
    ~3.5e12; beyond that the heavy BL pocket's k_F approaches kmax and the curve folds."""
    kg = np.linspace(1e3, kmax, nk)
    Eb = aba_bands(kg, U)                                  # (6, nk) eV
    # density vs E_F: n(E_F)=sum_bands k_F^2/pi (g_s g_v = 4)
    EFs = np.linspace(0, 0.07, 1500)
    def density(EF):
        tot = 0.0
        for b in range(6):
            cross = np.where((Eb[b,:-1]-EF)*(Eb[b,1:]-EF) < 0)[0]
            for c in cross:
                kF = kg[c]
                # only electron pockets (band rising through EF)
                if Eb[b,c+1] > Eb[b,c]:
                    tot += kF**2/np.pi
        return tot
    nvals = np.array([density(ef) for ef in EFs])
    EF = np.interp(n_target, nvals, EFs)
    # extract FS at EF
    fs = []
    for b in range(6):
        cross = np.where((Eb[b,:-1]-EF)*(Eb[b,1:]-EF) < 0)[0]
        for c in cross:
            if Eb[b,c+1] > Eb[b,c]:
                kF = kg[c]
                fs.append((F_from_area(np.pi*kF**2), kF))
    return EF, sorted(fs)

# ---------------- ABC: MacDonald effective 2-band ----------------
# Table I (ABC trilayer): gamma0 set to 3.16 to fix energy scale
G0c, G1c, G2c, G3c, G4c, DELTAc = 3.16, 0.502, -0.0171, -0.377, -0.099, -0.0014  # eV
def vi(g): return np.sqrt(3)/2 * A0 * (g*E)/HBAR
V0,V3,V4 = vi(G0c), vi(G3c), vi(G4c)

def E_abc(kx, ky, ud=0.0):
    """ABC conduction-band energy E^+ (eV) at (kx,ky). ud = displacement (eV)."""
    p = HBAR*np.hypot(kx,ky)/E            # eV*s/m units folded: treat v*p in eV
    phi = np.arctan2(ky, kx)
    vp = V0*HBAR*np.hypot(kx,ky)/E        # v0*p in eV
    h_ch = vp**3 / G1c**2
    h_s  = DELTAc - 2*V0*V4*(HBAR*np.hypot(kx,ky)/E)**2/G1c
    h_tr = G2c/2 - 2*V0*V3*(HBAR*np.hypot(kx,ky)/E)**2/G1c
    h_gap = ud*(1 - (vp/G1c)**2)
    root = np.sqrt(h_ch**2 + h_tr**2 + h_gap**2 + 2*np.cos(3*phi)*h_ch*h_tr)
    return h_s + root

def abc_fs(n_target, ud=0.0, kmax=3e8, ng=601):
    """Count ABC FS topology + frequencies at density n_target (m^-2)."""
    kx = np.linspace(-kmax, kmax, ng); KX,KY = np.meshgrid(kx, kx)
    Egrid = E_abc(KX, KY, ud)
    dk = kx[1]-kx[0]
    # find EF: occupied area * (g/(2pi)^2) = n ; g=4
    EFs = np.linspace(Egrid.min(), Egrid.min()+0.05, 1500)
    areas = []
    for ef in EFs:
        occ = Egrid < ef
        areas.append(occ.sum()*dk*dk)
    nvals = 4*np.array(areas)/(2*np.pi)**2
    EF = np.interp(n_target, nvals, EFs)
    occ = Egrid < EF
    ncc, _ = label(occ)
    n_components = ncc.max()
    center_occ = occ[ng//2, ng//2]
    A_occ = occ.sum()*dk*dk
    # topology -> n distinct frequencies
    if center_occ and n_components == 1:
        topo, nfreq = "single", 1
    elif (not center_occ) and n_components == 1:
        topo, nfreq = "annulus", 2
    else:
        topo, nfreq = f"{n_components}-pocket", 1
    # representative frequency from total enclosed area (single pocket case)
    F_tot = F_from_area(A_occ)
    return EF, topo, n_components, nfreq, F_tot

# ---------------- run ----------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"VF(ABA) = {VF:.3e} m/s ; v0(ABC) = {V0:.3e} m/s\n")
    ns = np.array([0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0]) * 1e12 * 1e4   # m^-2
    print("=== ABA (D=0) ===  n[1e12]  EF[meV]  #FS  frequencies[T] (sorted)   sum[T]")
    for n in ns:
        EF, fs = aba_fs(n)
        freqs = [F for F,_ in fs]
        fstr = ", ".join(f"{F:5.1f}" for F in freqs)
        print(f"   {n/1e16:5.2f}     {EF*1e3:6.1f}   {len(fs)}   [{fstr}]   {sum(freqs):5.1f}")
    print("\n=== ABC (D=0) ===  n[1e12]  EF[meV]  topo        #cc  #freq  F_tot[T]")
    for n in ns:
        EF, topo, ncc, nfreq, Ft = abc_fs(n)
        print(f"   {n/1e16:5.2f}     {EF*1e3:6.1f}   {topo:10s}  {ncc}    {nfreq}     {Ft:5.1f}")
    # D check for ABA at n=1e12: does the small ML pocket survive finite D?
    print("\n=== ABA at n=1e12, vs displacement U ===  U[meV]  #FS  frequencies[T]")
    for U in (0.0, 0.005, 0.010, 0.020, 0.040):
        EF, fs = aba_fs(1e16, U=U)
        print(f"   {U*1e3:5.0f}   {len(fs)}   [{', '.join(f'{F:.2f}' for F,_ in fs)}]")

1	# Landau fan
2	
3	## What
4	2D map of carrier density × magnetic field at fixed displacement field: `mag.field` as the **slow** axis of a `multimegasweep`, with a paired-(k_tg, k_bg) n-line (fixed D, via `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`) as the **fast** axis:
5	```python
6	s.multimegasweep([mag.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)
7	```
8	Field is slow because gates are cheap to retrace and the magnet is not — the magnet ramps once, monotonically, across the whole fan. Every lock-in X/P read at each grid point. Analysis side plots B vs n (`pcolormesh`) per contact pair and overlays Středa lines (see Verify). Distinct from its two neighbors: `field-sweep-1d` is one gate point with full B-axis density; `gatemap-in-field` is the full 2D gate plane at a *single* B. The fan trades both for the (n, B) plane — the only measurement that resolves how gapped states *disperse* with field.
9	
10	## When
11	Three triggers, in rough campaign order:
12	- **Oscillation check** — a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap-in-field` showed quantum-oscillation-like wiggles and you need to know if they're real. The corpus idiom is literally named for this: RPL_19's "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" (a 161 × 151 fan after an effective-mass series kept hinting at SdH). A feature that moves systematically across the n-line as B steps is physics; one that doesn't is noise or gate drift.
13	- **State classification** — a map shows a vanishing-ρxx region (or a busy set of dips) and the discriminating question is whether the features disperse. This is the classification backbone of an FQAH/SC-style campaign (arXiv 2504.06972: ρxx(ν_h, B) fans + Středa fits are how (R/F/I)QAH states were separated from the SC region).
14	- **Calibration** — SdH/LL frequency vs n gives cap ratios independently of the CNP-slope method, and for a moiré device the fan anchors the moiré density n_M. The extraction is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written); the fan is its input data.
15	
16	Prerequisites are `nD-map`'s plus a field-verified magnet: cap ratios `dtg`/`dbg` must be trusted (the fast axis is a line in (n, D) — wrong caps tilt it), and the field source must be live (Yokogawa cache seeded after kernel restart, AMI430 in operating mode — see `field-sweep-1d` plumbing notes).
17	
18	## Why
19	A dip in ρxx at one B value is ambiguous — gap, SC, contact artifact, density wobble. The same dip tracked across a fan is nearly unambiguous: a gapped state at fixed filling traces a straight line in (n, B) whose slope *is* its Chern number (Středa: dn/dB = C·e/h), an SC pocket sits at fixed n and dies at moderate B without dispersing, and quantum oscillations fan out with 1/B periodicity that yields the Fermi-surface area. One measurement, three discriminations, plus calibration for free.
20	
21	The cost is real: these are the most expensive sweeps in the corpus. Reference wall-clocks *(our-measurement, toploader, non-blocking-magnet era — the formula below them omits the traverse term; do not carry these numbers to another rig untagged)*: RPL_10's 101 B × 101 n fan at `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1` took **4.3 h** (file 156); the 351 × 251 version took **27.8 h** (file 159); RPL_19's 161 × 151 at `fast_delay=0.6` took **5.5 h** (file 1776 — Aaron's own `# 1776, took 5.5 hours` annotation propagates through later fan cells); the 441 × 231 fan to 5 T took **30.1 h** (file 1840). Aaron's inline arithmetic (`(351*501)/(201*151)*3` in 20260124 cell 134) is the toploader-era form.
22	
23	**Estimate before you run — the full cost model**: wall-clock = **field-traverse time + N_rows × (row turnaround + N_fast × per-point time)**. Which term dominates is a rig property, not a constant of nature: **if the field source is ramp-rate-limited and the set call blocks** (check the rig card for whether yours is), the traverse term is fixed by the B-span alone — **finer B steps cost only row turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time**. Traverses come in two species, priced differently: a **bare ramp** moves at the magnet's ramp rate; a **measured traverse** (the same leg recorded as a sweep) moves at an effective rate degraded by per-point overhead. A "free" measured ramp-down is usually still worth taking — it buys data for wall-clock — but it is not free: price it at the measured rate, from the rig card's Timing rules (`rig_card.md`), never the bare one. Calibrate row turnaround and per-point time from this session's own first sweeps; inherited timing constants carry a provenance tag and the conditions they were measured under, or they are guesses.
24	
25	## Recipe
26	1. Pick the n-window and fixed D from the map that motivated the fan, and decide the B span. Corpus shapes: oscillation check 0.9 → 2.5 T over a 151-pt n-line; classification fan 0 → 2.5 T, 251 × 151; deep fan 0.6 → 5 T, 441 × 231; high-field 5 → 12 T, 351 × 201. Start coarse (≤200 B steps, ≤151 n points); zoom only on confirmed structure. **Grid Nyquist check, both axes, at design time**: against the finest expected feature spacing in the analysis window — for SdH/LL structure the B-period at fixed n is ΔB ≈ (g·e/h)·B²/n (g = level degeneracy, 4 for spin×valley); evaluate at the **lowest-B, highest-n corner** of the hunt window and require ≥2 (prefer 3) rows per period, and the analogous check on the n-axis (ray spacing Δn = g·(e/h)·B at the lowest B you intend to read). An undersampled axis produces in-data aliasing that mimics curved structure and survives re-plotting; no post-hoc check fully recovers it. "Start coarse" applies to the *window*, never below the Nyquist floor of the structure you intend to claim — and where the cost model says fine B is nearly free (blocking ramp-limited magnets), take it. **Re-run this check whenever n_max changes — never inherit a ΔB across fans.** The B-period ΔB ∝ B²/n shrinks as n grows, so a ΔB that was Nyquist-OK for an n≤4 fan can undersample an n=10 firming fan at the same B (our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-14: ΔB=0.1 T gave 2.2 rows/period at n=4 but only 1.5 — under the ≥2 floor — at n=10, B=4 T; the undersampled corner is exactly where a spurious high-n second pocket appeared and had to be killed post-hoc). Where the rig makes fine B *not* free (measurement-dominated fans, e.g. a non-blocking-magnet rig at >1 s/pt — check the cost model), buy the high-n Nyquist floor by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n claim at B ≥ 5–6 T**, not by coarsening B.
27	2. Build the fast axis: `ns = np.linspace(n_hi, n_lo, N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(len(ns)); Vtgs, Vbgs = calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. A non-uniform n-vector is legitimate when you know where the action is — RPL_19's elevated-T fan stitches `np.hstack((n1, n2, n3))` with the dense segment over the CSC window and coarse segments elsewhere, with `#`-comments labeling each segment (20260124 cell 239).
28	3. Set lock-in sensitivity and time constant *before* the fan — at high B the resistance scale can be 10–100× the zero-field value and autorange-mid-fan ruins row-to-row comparability. RPL_19/20260217 cell 124 is the idiom: `sr830_N.sensitivity(10e-3)`, `sr830_N.time_constant(300e-3)` as an explicit pre-cell. Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
29	4. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended. A descending non-uniform `field_vec = np.hstack((np.linspace(12, 3, 181), np.linspace(3, 0, 151)))` packs steps densely where LLs are closely spaced (20260217 cell 96).
30	5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. The recipe asks for the RPL_10 discipline.
31	6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).
32	7. The sweep (step 0 call above). Delay band in the corpus: `slow_delay=1` (gates retrace during it; the field step itself is rate-limited by the magnet), `fast_delay` 0.5–1.0 s matching the time-constant ladder.
33	8. Park gates (`k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`), decide the field endpoint deliberately (leave it for a follow-up fan, `s.ramp(mag.field, 0)`, or ride home as a measured traverse — a free `field-sweep-1d`, priced at the measured rate per the Why cost model), and ping (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) — at 5–30 h these runs outlive operator attention spans.
34	
35	## Verify
36	Disk-side checks, then the Středa read. The fan is unrolled into flat rows; the slow column is `magnet_field`.
37	
38	```python
39	from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
40	import numpy as np
41	
42	run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
43	print(summarize_run(run))
44	# expect: type 2D, recipe 'landau-fan', slow_param ['magnet_field'],
45	#         fast_param ['k_tg_volt', 'k_bg_volt'].
46	
47	# 1. Completeness — at 5-30 h these are the most interruption-prone sweeps
48	#    in the corpus (RPL_10 file 158 and TD48-era runs died early; Aaron
49	#    re-ran rather than salvaged).
50	assert not run.interrupted, "fan was interrupted; decide re-run vs salvage with the human"
51	
52	# 2. B axis actually traversed the plan, monotonically per segment.
53	B = run.col("magnet_field")
54	print(f"B traversed: {B.min():.3f} → {B.max():.3f} T over {len(run.meta['slow_setpoints'][0])} steps")
55	
56	# 3. Fast axis is a paired n-line: both gate columns move together.
57	vtg, vbg = run.col("k_tg_volt"), run.col("k_bg_volt")
58	assert np.ptp(vtg) > 0 and np.ptp(vbg) > 0, "one gate is frozen — not a paired n-line"
59	
60	# 4. Temperature stayed at base across the fan (a 30 h run spans fridge
61	#    events). NOTE: 20260124-era RPL_19 data has TWO columns literally
62	#    named 'T' (probe + fridge); later sessions rename to T_probe/T_fridge.
63	#    run.col('T') raises on the duplicate — use col_indices/col_at.
64	for tname in ("T_probe", "T"):
65	    idxs = run.col_indices(tname)
66	    if idxs:
67	        T = run.col_at(idxs[0])
68	        print(f"{tname}: {np.nanmin(T)*1e3:.0f}–{np.nanmax(T)*1e3:.0f} mK")
69	        break
70	
71	# 5. Lock-ins not flat/NaN (same as gatemap). Gate-current columns are
72	#    usually ABSENT in fan data (plot-only, step 6) — skip, don't fail.
73	for name in set(run.cols):
74	    if name.startswith("sr830_") and name.endswith("_X"):
75	        x = run.col_at(run.col_indices(name)[0])
76	        if np.allclose(x, x[0]) or np.isnan(x).any():
77	            print(f"⚠️  {name} flat or NaN — check sensitivity/wiring")
78	```
79	
80	**Středa read** (the point of the fan): track ρxx dip positions n_dip(B) per B-row and fit dn/dB per dip family.
81	- A linearly dispersing dip is a gapped state with Chern number `C = (h/e) · dn/dB` (n in absolute units). The corpus tools are inline in the ana notebooks: `streda()` returning `B = phi0 * n / C` (RPL_19/20251220_ana cells 96–98) and the overlay form `x_fit = C * y_fit * 1E-16 / (h/e)` plotted over the file-1840 fan (20260124_ana cell 93, C = 1 dashed line with the constants from the boilerplate cell 3).
82	- **Moiré devices**: the slope converts to a Chern number only through the moiré density — `C = (h/e) · n_M · dν_h/dB`. The corpus has no ν_h layer; anchoring n_M and the ν_h↔n conversion is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written). Until it exists, report slopes in raw dn/dB and flag the assignment.
83	- **Do not hard-code "plateau value ⇒ Středa slope"** [flagged for expert review]: the RIQAH states in arXiv 2504.06972 show ρxy quantized at h/e² while their ρxx dips disperse with slopes near their *fractional filling*, not C = 1 — explicitly unexplained in that paper. A plateau/dispersion mismatch is an escalate-to-expert finding, not a fit error.
84	- **Fan onset as a quality metric**: the lowest B at which oscillations/LL dips resolve tracks quantum mobility — RPL_10's fans resolved structure below 1 T; RPL_19's oscillation check needed 0.9–2.5 T. A later cooldown whose onset field moves up is a device-quality regression worth noting.
85	
86	## Examples
87	- `aaron/RPL_10/241230_measure.ipynb` cells 50–53 — the original fans, exemplary comment discipline. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the index synopsis lumps these under "n-vs-B sweeps at D = 0.31" (cells 49–53); within that, cell 51 is a strict 1D field sweep (claimed by `field-sweep-1d` Examples, which already flags 50/52/53 as "landau-fan-shaped") and cell 54 is a *raw, never-executed* draft fan at D = 0.25. The executed fans: cell 50 → file 156 (101 B × 101 n, B 1→0 T, `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1`, 4.3 h), cell 52 → file 158 (351 × 201 — **interrupted at 0.0 h** and immediately superseded), cell 53 → file 159 (351 × 251, 27.8 h, the fan the qo-discovery fixture freezes on). Note B runs *downward* (1→0): the magnet was parked at 1 T by the preceding `## Gate maps in field` cells 46–48, so the fan starts where the magnet sits.

# Landau fan

## What
2D map of carrier density × magnetic field at fixed displacement field: `mag.field` as the **slow** axis of a `multimegasweep`, with a paired-(k_tg, k_bg) n-line (fixed D, via `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`) as the **fast** axis:
```python
s.multimegasweep([mag.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)
```
Field is slow because gates are cheap to retrace and the magnet is not — the magnet ramps once, monotonically, across the whole fan. Every lock-in X/P read at each grid point. Analysis side plots B vs n (`pcolormesh`) per contact pair and overlays Středa lines (see Verify). Distinct from its two neighbors: `field-sweep-1d` is one gate point with full B-axis density; `gatemap-in-field` is the full 2D gate plane at a *single* B. The fan trades both for the (n, B) plane — the only measurement that resolves how gapped states *disperse* with field.

## When
Three triggers, in rough campaign order:
- **Oscillation check** — a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap-in-field` showed quantum-oscillation-like wiggles and you need to know if they're real. The corpus idiom is literally named for this: RPL_19's "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" (a 161 × 151 fan after an effective-mass series kept hinting at SdH). A feature that moves systematically across the n-line as B steps is physics; one that doesn't is noise or gate drift.
- **State classification** — a map shows a vanishing-ρxx region (or a busy set of dips) and the discriminating question is whether the features disperse. This is the classification backbone of an FQAH/SC-style campaign (arXiv 2504.06972: ρxx(ν_h, B) fans + Středa fits are how (R/F/I)QAH states were separated from the SC region).
- **Calibration** — SdH/LL frequency vs n gives cap ratios independently of the CNP-slope method, and for a moiré device the fan anchors the moiré density n_M. The extraction is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written); the fan is its input data.

Prerequisites are `nD-map`'s plus a field-verified magnet: cap ratios `dtg`/`dbg` must be trusted (the fast axis is a line in (n, D) — wrong caps tilt it), and the field source must be live (Yokogawa cache seeded after kernel restart, AMI430 in operating mode — see `field-sweep-1d` plumbing notes).

## Why
A dip in ρxx at one B value is ambiguous — gap, SC, contact artifact, density wobble. The same dip tracked across a fan is nearly unambiguous: a gapped state at fixed filling traces a straight line in (n, B) whose slope *is* its Chern number (Středa: dn/dB = C·e/h), an SC pocket sits at fixed n and dies at moderate B without dispersing, and quantum oscillations fan out with 1/B periodicity that yields the Fermi-surface area. One measurement, three discriminations, plus calibration for free.

The cost is real: these are the most expensive sweeps in the corpus. Reference wall-clocks *(our-measurement, toploader, non-blocking-magnet era — the formula below them omits the traverse term; do not carry these numbers to another rig untagged)*: RPL_10's 101 B × 101 n fan at `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1` took **4.3 h** (file 156); the 351 × 251 version took **27.8 h** (file 159); RPL_19's 161 × 151 at `fast_delay=0.6` took **5.5 h** (file 1776 — Aaron's own `# 1776, took 5.5 hours` annotation propagates through later fan cells); the 441 × 231 fan to 5 T took **30.1 h** (file 1840). Aaron's inline arithmetic (`(351*501)/(201*151)*3` in 20260124 cell 134) is the toploader-era form.

**Estimate before you run — the full cost model**: wall-clock = **field-traverse time + N_rows × (row turnaround + N_fast × per-point time)**. Which term dominates is a rig property, not a constant of nature: **if the field source is ramp-rate-limited and the set call blocks** (check the rig card for whether yours is), the traverse term is fixed by the B-span alone — **finer B steps cost only row turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time**. Traverses come in two species, priced differently: a **bare ramp** moves at the magnet's ramp rate; a **measured traverse** (the same leg recorded as a sweep) moves at an effective rate degraded by per-point overhead. A "free" measured ramp-down is usually still worth taking — it buys data for wall-clock — but it is not free: price it at the measured rate, from the rig card's Timing rules (`rig_card.md`), never the bare one. Calibrate row turnaround and per-point time from this session's own first sweeps; inherited timing constants carry a provenance tag and the conditions they were measured under, or they are guesses.

## Recipe
1. Pick the n-window and fixed D from the map that motivated the fan, and decide the B span. Corpus shapes: oscillation check 0.9 → 2.5 T over a 151-pt n-line; classification fan 0 → 2.5 T, 251 × 151; deep fan 0.6 → 5 T, 441 × 231; high-field 5 → 12 T, 351 × 201. Start coarse (≤200 B steps, ≤151 n points); zoom only on confirmed structure. **Grid Nyquist check, both axes, at design time**: against the finest expected feature spacing in the analysis window — for SdH/LL structure the B-period at fixed n is ΔB ≈ (g·e/h)·B²/n (g = level degeneracy, 4 for spin×valley); evaluate at the **lowest-B, highest-n corner** of the hunt window and require ≥2 (prefer 3) rows per period, and the analogous check on the n-axis (ray spacing Δn = g·(e/h)·B at the lowest B you intend to read). An undersampled axis produces in-data aliasing that mimics curved structure and survives re-plotting; no post-hoc check fully recovers it. "Start coarse" applies to the *window*, never below the Nyquist floor of the structure you intend to claim — and where the cost model says fine B is nearly free (blocking ramp-limited magnets), take it. **Re-run this check whenever n_max changes — never inherit a ΔB across fans.** The B-period ΔB ∝ B²/n shrinks as n grows, so a ΔB that was Nyquist-OK for an n≤4 fan can undersample an n=10 firming fan at the same B (our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-14: ΔB=0.1 T gave 2.2 rows/period at n=4 but only 1.5 — under the ≥2 floor — at n=10, B=4 T; the undersampled corner is exactly where a spurious high-n second pocket appeared and had to be killed post-hoc). Where the rig makes fine B *not* free (measurement-dominated fans, e.g. a non-blocking-magnet rig at >1 s/pt — check the cost model), buy the high-n Nyquist floor by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n claim at B ≥ 5–6 T**, not by coarsening B.
2. Build the fast axis: `ns = np.linspace(n_hi, n_lo, N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(len(ns)); Vtgs, Vbgs = calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. A non-uniform n-vector is legitimate when you know where the action is — RPL_19's elevated-T fan stitches `np.hstack((n1, n2, n3))` with the dense segment over the CSC window and coarse segments elsewhere, with `#`-comments labeling each segment (20260124 cell 239).
3. Set lock-in sensitivity and time constant *before* the fan — at high B the resistance scale can be 10–100× the zero-field value and autorange-mid-fan ruins row-to-row comparability. RPL_19/20260217 cell 124 is the idiom: `sr830_N.sensitivity(10e-3)`, `sr830_N.time_constant(300e-3)` as an explicit pre-cell. Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
4. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended. A descending non-uniform `field_vec = np.hstack((np.linspace(12, 3, 181), np.linspace(3, 0, 151)))` packs steps densely where LLs are closely spaced (20260217 cell 96).
5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. The recipe asks for the RPL_10 discipline.
6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).
7. The sweep (step 0 call above). Delay band in the corpus: `slow_delay=1` (gates retrace during it; the field step itself is rate-limited by the magnet), `fast_delay` 0.5–1.0 s matching the time-constant ladder.
8. Park gates (`k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`), decide the field endpoint deliberately (leave it for a follow-up fan, `s.ramp(mag.field, 0)`, or ride home as a measured traverse — a free `field-sweep-1d`, priced at the measured rate per the Why cost model), and ping (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) — at 5–30 h these runs outlive operator attention spans.

## Verify
Disk-side checks, then the Středa read. The fan is unrolled into flat rows; the slow column is `magnet_field`.

```python
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
import numpy as np

run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
print(summarize_run(run))
# expect: type 2D, recipe 'landau-fan', slow_param ['magnet_field'],
#         fast_param ['k_tg_volt', 'k_bg_volt'].

# 1. Completeness — at 5-30 h these are the most interruption-prone sweeps
#    in the corpus (RPL_10 file 158 and TD48-era runs died early; Aaron
#    re-ran rather than salvaged).
assert not run.interrupted, "fan was interrupted; decide re-run vs salvage with the human"

# 2. B axis actually traversed the plan, monotonically per segment.
B = run.col("magnet_field")
print(f"B traversed: {B.min():.3f} → {B.max():.3f} T over {len(run.meta['slow_setpoints'][0])} steps")

# 3. Fast axis is a paired n-line: both gate columns move together.
vtg, vbg = run.col("k_tg_volt"), run.col("k_bg_volt")
assert np.ptp(vtg) > 0 and np.ptp(vbg) > 0, "one gate is frozen — not a paired n-line"

# 4. Temperature stayed at base across the fan (a 30 h run spans fridge
#    events). NOTE: 20260124-era RPL_19 data has TWO columns literally
#    named 'T' (probe + fridge); later sessions rename to T_probe/T_fridge.
#    run.col('T') raises on the duplicate — use col_indices/col_at.
for tname in ("T_probe", "T"):
    idxs = run.col_indices(tname)
    if idxs:
        T = run.col_at(idxs[0])
        print(f"{tname}: {np.nanmin(T)*1e3:.0f}–{np.nanmax(T)*1e3:.0f} mK")
        break

# 5. Lock-ins not flat/NaN (same as gatemap). Gate-current columns are
#    usually ABSENT in fan data (plot-only, step 6) — skip, don't fail.
for name in set(run.cols):
    if name.startswith("sr830_") and name.endswith("_X"):
        x = run.col_at(run.col_indices(name)[0])
        if np.allclose(x, x[0]) or np.isnan(x).any():
```

import numpy as np, json
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
import scipy.constants as cst

m=json.load(open("data/1/metadata.json")); idx={c:i for i,c in enumerate(m["columns"])}
d=np.loadtxt("data/1/data.tsv.gz")
nfast=101; nr=d.shape[0]//nfast; d=d[:nr*nfast].reshape(nr,nfast,-1)
bg=d[:,0,idx["k_bg_volt"]]; tg=d[0,:,idx["DC_bias"]]
I_bias=5e-9
print(f"map {nr} BG rows x {nfast} TG pts; BG[{bg.min():.2f},{bg.max():.2f}] TG[{tg.min():.2f},{tg.max():.2f}]")

# Geometry-prior capacitances (SiO2 term zeroed) — c_tg anchored to stack prior.
eps0=cst.epsilon_0; kap=3.0
c_tg = eps0*kap/15.6e-9
c_bg_geom = eps0*kap/12e-9
print(f"geom: c_tg={c_tg:.4e} F/m^2  c_bg_geom={c_bg_geom:.4e}  ratio_geom(c_bg/c_tg)={c_bg_geom/c_tg:.3f}")

def ridge(Rname):
    R=np.abs(d[:,:,idx[Rname]])/I_bias
    tg_cnp=np.full(nr,np.nan)
    pred=-1.30*bg   # geometry-prior seed for continuity window
    for r in range(nr):
        sm=gaussian_filter1d(R[r],2.0)
        # continuity window: +/-2V around prediction (avoid competing maxima)
        win=np.abs(tg-pred[r])<2.0
        if win.sum()<5: continue
        j=np.where(win)[0][np.argmax(sm[win])]
        if j<=1 or j>=nfast-2:   # edge-clipped -> exclude
            continue
        tg_cnp[r]=tg[j]
    return tg_cnp,R

res={}
fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(13,5))
for k,(nm,col) in enumerate([("sr1 T3-T4","sr1_X"),("sr2 B4-B5","sr2_X")]):
    tg_cnp,R=ridge(col)
    ok=~np.isnan(tg_cnp)
    p=np.polyfit(bg[ok],tg_cnp[ok],1)   # tg_cnp = p[0]*bg + p[1]
    resid=tg_cnp[ok]-np.polyval(p,bg[ok])
    ratio=-p[0]
    res[nm]=dict(slope=p[0],intercept=p[1],ratio=ratio,rms=resid.std(),n=ok.sum())
    print(f"\n{nm}: rows used {ok.sum()}/{nr}  slope dVtg/dVbg={p[0]:.4f} intercept={p[1]:+.4f} V")
    print(f"   -> c_bg/c_tg = -slope = {ratio:.3f}  (geom 1.30)  ridge-fit RMS={resid.std()*1e3:.1f} mV")
    im=ax[k].pcolormesh(bg,tg,np.log10(np.clip(R.T,1,None)),shading="auto",cmap="viridis")
    ax[k].plot(bg[ok],tg_cnp[ok],"r.",ms=4,label="CNP ridge")
    ax[k].plot(bg,np.polyval(p,bg),"w--",lw=1,label=f"fit slope {p[0]:.2f}")
    ax[k].set_xlabel("BG (V)"); ax[k].set_ylabel("TG / DC_bias (V)")
    ax[k].set_title(f"{nm}  log10 Rxx"); ax[k].legend(loc="upper right",fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/gatemap_cnp.png",dpi=110)
print("\nsaved hera_scratch/gatemap_cnp.png")

# Cross-channel agreement
rr=[res[k]["ratio"] for k in res]
print(f"\ncross-channel ratio: {rr[0]:.3f} vs {rr[1]:.3f}  (delta {abs(rr[0]-rr[1]):.3f})")

# Adopt averaged ratio (channels agree); derive c_bg; offsets from sr1 fit.
ratio=np.mean(rr); c_bg=ratio*c_tg
def calc_nD(Vtg,Vbg,n_off=0,D_off=0):
    n=(c_tg*Vtg+c_bg*Vbg)/cst.e + n_off
    D=0.5*(c_tg*Vtg-c_bg*Vbg)/eps0 + D_off
    return n,D
b_int=res["sr1 T3-T4"]["intercept"]   # Vtg at Vbg=0 on the CNP line
n_off=-calc_nD(b_int,0)[0]
print(f"\nadopted ratio {ratio:.3f}  c_bg={c_bg:.4e}  n_offset={n_off:.3e} m^-2")
# closure: n along fitted ridge ~ 0
tg_line=np.polyval([res["sr1 T3-T4"]["slope"],b_int],bg)
nline,Dline=calc_nD(tg_line,bg,n_off)
print(f"closure: max|n| on ridge = {np.abs(nline).max():.3e} m^-2 ({np.abs(nline).max()/1e16:.3f}e12 cm^-2)")
print(f"n per V along D=0: {2*c_tg/cst.e/1e4:.3e} cm^-2/V (TG, D=0 matched)")

```python
import os

def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()


def load1d(i):
    return np.loadtxt(os.path.join(file_path, "{:d}".format(i), "data.tsv.gz"))

def load_meta(i):
    fp = open(os.path.join(file_path, "{:d}".format(i), "metadata.json"), "r")
    return json.load(fp)

def pretty_load(i):
    data = load1d(i)
    meta = load_meta(i)

    for ind, col in enumerate(meta['columns']):

    meta = load_meta(i)
```

```python
def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
```

from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d

# --- load the 0 T gate map (file_id 1) ---
mD = load_meta(1); cols = mD['columns']; ci = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(cols)}
raw = load1d(1); nfast = 101; nr = raw.shape[0] // nfast
g = raw[:nr*nfast].reshape(nr, nfast, -1)
bg = g[:, 0, ci['k_bg_volt']]; tg = g[0, :, ci['DC_bias']]
I_bias = 5e-9

def ridge(col):
    """Smoothed-argmax CNP ridge per BG row, windowed to the continuous ridge
    (geometry-prior seed) and excluding edge-clipped rows."""
    R = np.abs(g[:, :, ci[col]]) / I_bias
    pred = -1.30 * bg; out = np.full(nr, np.nan)
    for r in range(nr):
        win = np.abs(tg - pred[r]) < 2.0
        j = np.where(win)[0][np.argmax(gaussian_filter1d(R[r], 2.0)[win])]
        if 1 < j < nfast - 2:
            out[r] = tg[j]
    return out, R

fits = {}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))
for k, (nm, col) in enumerate([('sr1 T3-T4', 'sr1_X'), ('sr2 B4-B5', 'sr2_X')]):
    rc, R = ridge(col); ok = ~np.isnan(rc)
    p = np.polyfit(bg[ok], rc[ok], 1); ratio = -p[0]
    rms = (rc[ok] - np.polyval(p, bg[ok])).std()
    fits[nm] = (p[0], p[1], ratio, rms)
    print(f"{nm}: slope {p[0]:.4f}  intercept {p[1]:+.4f} V  c_bg/c_tg={ratio:.3f}"
          f"  RMS {rms*1e3:.1f} mV  (rows {ok.sum()}/{nr})")
    ax[k].pcolormesh(bg, tg, np.log10(np.clip(R.T, 1, None)), shading='auto', cmap='viridis')
    ax[k].plot(bg[ok], rc[ok], 'r.', ms=4, label='CNP ridge')
    ax[k].plot(bg, np.polyval(p, bg), 'w--', lw=1, label=f'fit {p[0]:.2f}')
    ax[k].set_xlabel('BG (V)'); ax[k].set_ylabel('TG / DC_bias (V)')
    ax[k].set_title(f'{nm}  log10 Rxx + CNP fit'); ax[k].legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# --- adopt calibration: RATIO data-calibrated; SCALE geometry-prior ---
ratio = float(np.mean([fits[k][2] for k in fits]))
c_tg_cal = calc_ctg(15.6e-9)               # anchored to 15.6 nm hBN stack prior
c_bg_cal = ratio * c_tg_cal
b_int = fits['sr1 T3-T4'][1]
n_offset_cal = -calc_nD(b_int, 0, c_tg_cal, c_bg_cal)[0]
D_offset_cal = 0.0
print(f"\ncross-channel ratio agreement: {fits['sr1 T3-T4'][2]:.3f} vs {fits['sr2 B4-B5'][2]:.3f}")
print(f"ADOPTED  c_bg/c_tg={ratio:.3f}  c_tg={c_tg_cal:.4e}  c_bg={c_bg_cal:.4e} F/m^2")
print(f"         n_offset={n_offset_cal:.3e} m^-2  D_offset={D_offset_cal}")
print("provenance: RATIO data-calibrated (file_id 1); SCALE geometry prior (15.6 nm hBN),"
      " pending QH lever-arm upgrade from the fan")
tg_line = np.polyval([fits['sr1 T3-T4'][0], b_int], bg)
n_ridge = calc_nD(tg_line, bg, c_tg_cal, c_bg_cal, n_offset_cal)[0]
print(f"closure: max|n| on fitted ridge = {np.abs(n_ridge).max():.2e} m^-2"
      f" ({np.abs(n_ridge).max()/1e16:.3f}e12 cm^-2)")
print(f"density lever (D=0): {2*c_tg_cal/cst_e/1e4:.3e} cm^-2 per V (TG, BG matched)")

Operational log per the HERA agent prompt. Streams: RECIPE FIX / TOOLING /
PROTOCOL / FEEDBACK. First autonomous (E1) session — tooling/protocol
friction is a primary deliverable.
